title: Move-out cleaning in Greer: floors, baseboards and edges
description: Move out cleaning floors Greer SC: how baseboards, floor edges, tracks and door bottoms get cleaned for a deposit-ready home. Free in-home estimate first.

takeaways: Floors and edges are where move-out inspections find the most dirt, because furniture hid it for years.
The order matters: top-down, detail the edges, and mop last, working toward the door.

html:
Ask a property manager what gets a deposit deduction in Greer and the answer is rarely the oven. It is the floor along the wall, the baseboard with a gray fuzz line, and the corner behind the bedroom door. Move out cleaning on floors in Greer, SC is mostly an edge job, and the edges are where a quick mop never goes.

Below is how the order of work goes when we do the floors and trim in an empty home, with the questions we hear most from renters and sellers.

Why do the edges matter more than the middle?

Because the middle of a floor is what everyone cleans. A vacuum passes down the center, a mop follows, and the room looks fine from the doorway. Then someone kneels or looks along the baseboard in raking light from a window, and the line of dust and dried grime shows up. A final inspection is exactly that kind of look.

Perfect Services is a Brazilian-owned team, and the part of our method that people notice first is hand-washing along the walls instead of running a mop head past them. The same attention is built into our move-out cleaning in Greer, where floors are vacuumed and mopped edge to edge.

The order we work in

  1. Top first. Door frames, switches and window sills get wiped before the floor, so nothing falls onto a clean surface later.
  2. Baseboards. Wiped by hand along their full length, room by room, including behind doors and around closet openings.
  3. Closet floors. Shelves and rods first, then the floor underneath them.
  4. Vacuum the whole floor, edges and corners with a tool, then the open area.
  5. Mop hard floors, starting in the far corner and working back toward the exit, so we never walk across wet floor.
  6. Final look along each wall with the lights on and the blinds open.

Moving toward the door is a small detail, but it is the kind of thing that keeps a finished floor finished.

What changes by floor type?

Homes around Greer, Taylors and Duncan have a mix of hardwood, tile, vinyl plank and carpet, often in the same house. Each needs something different.

FloorWhat we look forCare
HardwoodGrit that scratches, water-sensitive seamsThorough vacuuming first, then a damp, not wet, wash
Tile and groutDark grout lines, dried spills near the kitchenHand-washing along the grout, extra time near bathrooms
Vinyl plankScuffs and residue from rugs or matsGentle mopping with attention to seams at the edges
CarpetPet hair along walls, traffic lanes, stainsDetailed vacuuming; stains and odors discussed at the estimate

Baseboards, door bottoms and the places a mop skips

Baseboards are the most common deduction we hear about, and they take longer than people expect. The top edge holds dust, the face holds scuffs, and the bottom edge catches whatever the mop pushed along. In a three- or four-bedroom home that is a lot of linear feet.

The bottom of interior doors and their frames are the next spot. They sit at exactly the height where shoes, pets and vacuum bumpers make contact. Sliding glass door tracks come third. Pollen and red clay settle in them, and they almost always need a vacuum before any wiping.

Other spots that tend to be missed:

  • The strip of floor under where the refrigerator or washer stood.
  • Vent covers on the floor and their surrounding frame.
  • Stair edges and the corner where each step meets the wall.
  • Thresholds between rooms, where two floor types meet.
  • The floor of every closet, not only the shelves.

Should I clean the floors myself before you arrive?

You can sweep up loose debris, but you do not need to mop. Sweeping the big pieces helps, since screws, nails from hung pictures and bits of tape can scratch a hard floor when a machine rolls over them. Remove rugs and mats and take down anything taped to the wall. Beyond that, leave the real cleaning to the order above. If you want to compare how we treat other rooms, our guide to bedrooms and closets walks through the closet shelves and floors in more detail.

How much does floor-focused move-out cleaning cost?

We do not sell floors as a separate item. They are part of the full move-out, and the price depends on home size, the condition the last occupant left, whether the home is empty or furnished, and the timing of your move. A house with a lot of carpet and one large dog differs from an empty apartment with vinyl. For that reason Perfect Services gives prices only after a free in-home estimate. How long will it take, and can I book this week?

Floors and trim usually run alongside the kitchen and bathrooms, so a team splits the work. A larger home with many rooms takes longer, and a tight closing-day schedule may need more people. faqs: Do you clean baseboards by hand in a Greer move-out?
Yes. Baseboards, door frames and light switches are on the move-out checklist, and we wipe baseboards along their full length rather than only at the corners.
Will you mop hardwood floors with a lot of water?
No. Hardwood is handled differently from tile, with thorough vacuuming first and a damp wash. If you have a particular flooring concern, mention it at the free estimate.
What if my carpet has pet stains?
Tell us at the estimate. The move-out service covers detailed vacuuming, and we will explain what can be done about stains or odors before you decide anything.
